items.title: 13.3.2 Types of Animals on the basis ability of Thermoregulation

source_refs.note: Topic 13.3.2 with the side box (PDF 8). The claim that all invertebrates are poikilotherms is carried as printed (some insects warm their flight muscles); flagged.

items: Poikilotherms cannot keep their body temperature within narrow limits; it varies a lot, usually matching the environment. The book lists all invertebrates and the fishes, amphibians and reptiles.

Homeotherms keep a fairly constant internal temperature regardless of the environment, using a 'thermostat', the hypothalamus, to trigger cooling or warming. Mammals and birds are homeotherms; humans keep about 37 C in very cold or very hot surroundings.

blocks.text: Poikilotherms do not need to eat huge amounts of food to fuel a constant temperature, so they can survive in nutrient-poor places where a homeotherm would starve.

blocks.explanation: Homeotherms keep a nearly constant body temperature (birds, mammals) but need much food; poikilotherms let body temperature vary with the surroundings (fishes, reptiles) and need far less food.

items: Poikilotherms: variable temperature, less food. Homeotherms: constant temperature set by the hypothalamus.
